rows.basis: Revenue of the HPC Leasing segment (HPC lease revenue), the AI hosting line: 16,899,000 ÷ 168,455,000 total revenue. Digital asset (bitcoin mining) revenue of 151,556,000 is excluded; the GPUs belong to the tenants.

Consolidated capex of 1,060,189,000 (purchase of and deposits on plant and equipment) went mostly to the HPC build at Lake Mariner, but it is not split by segment. Construction in process rose from 107,624,000 to 1,069,059,000, and that category is not HPC-specific. The thesis notes a further $450.0m invested in the Abernathy JV, which is not in this pack. No AI amount is stated.

The company described HPC spend in words only: a 128-GPU NVIDIA cluster bought in Q2 (no dollar amount), interconnect, liquid-cooling and power-redundancy upgrades at Lake Mariner, and HPC data centers for Core42 of up to 72.5 MW. Consolidated capex was 267,940,000 with no HPC split.
The company dedicated a 2 MW block at Lake Mariner to generative AI/ML compute loads, with no amount stated. Consolidated capex of 75,168,000 was overwhelmingly mining.
The company referred to its 30% equity contribution for CB-1, a 20 MW (gross) liquid-cooled HPC/AI facility expected to be substantially complete by year-end, without stating an amount.

The company priced a $3.2bn offering of 7.750% senior secured notes due 2030 to finance construction of 522.5 MW of AI/HPC data centers at Lake Mariner, and the MD&A says capital allocation is now centered on HPC. The notes are financing, not capex guidance, and no 2026 capex dollar figure was given.

The company expected HPC hosting revenue to begin in Q2 2025 and announced leases worth $1bn of cumulative revenue over initial 10-year terms. That $1bn is a contract value over the term, not revenue for the year, so it is not used as an amount.
Management expects the revenue mix to keep shifting toward HPC leasing and away from bitcoin mining as contracted capacity is energized. No amount was given.

The Anthropic lease carries about $19bn of contracted revenue over the initial term, rising to about $33bn with both extensions. That is a project contract value over many years, not revenue for the fiscal year.
